problem.text: The example chat registry lacked a Dots prompt format. This change adds a selectable template, not a model architecture implementation.

reasoning.text: Registering 'dots' reuses the existing chat dispatch, conversation history, special-token encoding and generation loop instead of introducing a separate chat application.

impact.text: Selecting --mode dots supplies Dots role delimiters, disables added BOS, and supplies response-ending stop conditions and Dots-specific reasoning tags. Existing template entries remain unchanged.

source_notes.text: The earlier Cohere entry describes the same registry-based integration and optional-system/completed-versus-pending-turn pattern that the Dots formatter closely follows.

Issue #51, 'dots.llm1 support', was opened by louiehelm and requests model architecture support. Its relationship to this turboderp-authored template change is inferred from the shared Dots identifier; the issue does not establish that this commit fulfills that broader request.

limitations: No Dots model or tokenizer was executed; recognition of the marker tokens, generation quality and end-to-end stopping remain unverified.
The bounded Python check transcribed formatting logic; it did not execute the added class or the chat pipeline.

chapters.title: Dots chat formatting through the existing template interface

claims.text: PromptFormat_dots.format emits a system prompt only when truthy, enclosed by <|system|> and <|endofsystem|>. Each (user, answer) pair emits <|userprompt|>, user text, <|endofuserprompt|> and <|response|>. A non-None answer appends its text and <|endofresponse|>; None leaves the response prefix open for generation. No extra whitespace is inserted.

The default system prompt is 'You are a helpful assistant.' The chat caller uses that default unless a truthy custom system prompt is supplied. It appends a pending (user_prompt, None) pair before formatting and stores the generated answer back into that pair afterward, matching the new formatter's input contract.

add_bos returns False, while the existing caller still encodes special tokens. stop_conditions supplies the tokenizer EOS ID, the exact-token lookup for <|endofresponse|>, and that marker as a literal string. This follows the existing ChatML combination of token-ID and string stops. single_id performs dictionary lookup rather than validating that the marker exists.

thinktag returns <|sec-cot|> and <|sec-end-cot|>. The existing --think path appends the opening tag to the formatted prompt; --no_think passes both tags as banned strings. The same pair is passed to the streamer's formatting interface.

A standard-library Python transcription passed four assertions covering an exact completed-plus-pending conversation, omission of an empty system prompt, and the distinction between empty and absent answers. The example contained two response starts but only one response end.

annotation.summary: Adds an explicitly selectable Dots chat template with role delimiters, response stops and reasoning tags, reusing the existing chat pipeline.

argv:
def fmt(s, ms):
 c=''
 if s: c+='<|system|>'+s+'<|endofsystem|>'
 for u,a in ms:
  c+='<|userprompt|>'+u+'<|endofuserprompt|><|response|>'
  if a is not None: c+=a+'<|endofresponse|>'
 return c
x=fmt('S',[('U','A'),('V',None)])
assert x=='<|system|>S<|endofsystem|><|userprompt|>U<|endofuserprompt|><|response|>A<|endofresponse|><|userprompt|>V<|endofuserprompt|><|response|>'
assert fmt('',[('U','')]).endswith('<|response|><|endofresponse|>')
assert fmt('',[('U',None)]).endswith('<|response|>')
assert '<|system|>' not in fmt('',[('U',None)])
print('4 formatting assertions passed; completed+pending example: 2 response starts, 1 response end.')
